title: reliability-regimes: code, curated data and frozen outputs for "Bioactivity prediction error for compounds unlike their starting leads but close to measured analogs"

creators.name: Dong, Liang
creators.affiliation: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Baylor University, Waco, TX, USA

description: Code, curated data and frozen analysis outputs for a study of how far a bioactivity prediction can be assessed from two chemical reference sets: a compound's distance to the starting leads of a search, and its distance to the rest of the model's training data. An initial five-target panel relevant to therapy and molecular imaging (SCD-1 and FADS, endoplasmic-reticulum membrane lipid desaturases, and NK1R, DRD2 and DRD3, class A G-protein-coupled receptors) is followed by a validation on 11 additional protein targets spanning five class A GPCRs, two kinases, three other enzymes and one ion channel, and by time-split tests on eight dated targets. The study measures reliability within the pool the model was fitted from, under novelty-driven optimization, under temporal shift to chemistry published after the model was fitted, and under acquisition against measured activity. Every reported number is produced by a frozen analysis script run against a frozen output file and re-checked by verify_results.py, validation/check.py and temporal/verify.py, each of which exits non-zero on any mismatch.
